description: C++ programs for the D1 Mini ESP8266.

lessons.name: WiFi running light
lessons.description: A D1 Mini ESP8266 WiFi LED jackpot game with four colored LEDs. The LEDs run continuously for 30 seconds with 13 progressively slower speed stages, then the final LED becomes the jackpot color and blinks 5 times. The game round, running status, countdown, and winning color are automatically sent to Firebase Realtime Database.
lessons.connectionGuide:
WIFI FIREBASE LED JACKPOT - D1 MINI
=====================================

COMPONENTS:
- D1 Mini (ESP8266)
- Red LED
- Yellow LED
- Green LED
- Blue LED
- 4x Current-limiting resistors
- Jumper wires
- USB cable / suitable 5V power source
- WiFi connection
- Firebase Realtime Database

LED CONNECTIONS:

RED LED:
Anode (+)              -> D5 / GPIO 14 through resistor
Cathode (-)            -> GND

YELLOW LED:
Anode (+)              -> D6 / GPIO 12 through resistor
Cathode (-)            -> GND

GREEN LED:
Anode (+)              -> D7 / GPIO 13 through resistor
Cathode (-)            -> GND

BLUE LED:
Anode (+)              -> D3 / GPIO 0 through resistor
Cathode (-)            -> GND

PIN ASSIGNMENTS:
D5 -> RED LED
D6 -> YELLOW LED
D7 -> GREEN LED
D3 -> BLUE LED

HOW IT WORKS:
1. The D1 Mini connects to the configured WiFi network.
2. After connecting, it sends a READY status to Firebase.
3. A new game round starts automatically.
4. One of the four LEDs is randomly selected as the starting LED.
5. The LEDs run continuously for 30 seconds.
6. The running speed changes through 13 stages, becoming progressively slower.
7. At the end of the 30-second running period, the current LED becomes the jackpot color.
8. The winning color is sent to Firebase as the RESULT.
9. The winning LED blinks 5 times using a 500 ms ON and 500 ms OFF interval.
10. After the jackpot sequence finishes, the LEDs turn off and the next round starts automatically.

13 SPEED STAGES:
Stage 1  -> 10 ms   -> 0-3 seconds
Stage 2  -> 20 ms   -> 3-6 seconds
Stage 3  -> 40 ms   -> 6-9 seconds
Stage 4  -> 50 ms   -> 9-12 seconds
Stage 5  -> 80 ms   -> 12-15 seconds
Stage 6  -> 100 ms  -> 15-18 seconds
Stage 7  -> 200 ms  -> 18-21 seconds
Stage 8  -> 300 ms  -> 21-23 seconds
Stage 9  -> 500 ms  -> 23-25 seconds
Stage 10 -> 700 ms  -> 25-27 seconds
Stage 11 -> 900 ms  -> 27-28 seconds
Stage 12 -> 1200 ms -> 28-29 seconds
Stage 13 -> 1500 ms -> 29-30 seconds

FIREBASE DATA:
The D1 Mini sends game information to:
https://ccon-27175-default-rtdb.firebaseio.com/game.json

The Firebase game object contains:
- status: READY, RUNNING, or RESULT
- round: current round number
- countdown: countdown value
- result: winning color

IMPORTANT:
- The code uses the D1 Mini pin labels D5, D6, D7, and D3.
- Use a suitable resistor for each LED, commonly around 220-330 ohms.
- Connect all LED cathodes to GND.
- The D1 Mini must have access to the configured WiFi network for Firebase updates.
- If the WiFi connection is unavailable, the LED game can continue running, but Firebase updates will not be sent.
- Make sure the Firebase Realtime Database URL matches the database used by the web application.
- The WiFi credentials are stored directly in the source code and should be changed before distributing the code.

lessons.name: Automatic Pet Feeder
lessons.description: Dispense pet food using a servo motor with a push button trigger. The servo opens the food dispenser, waits for a few seconds, then automatically closes it.
lessons.connectionGuide:
AUTOMATIC PET FEEDER - D1 MINI
==============================

COMPONENTS:
- D1 Mini (ESP8266)
- Servo Motor
- Push Button
- Jumper Wires

SERVO MOTOR:
Signal (Orange/Yellow) -> D5 / GPIO 14
VCC (Red)              -> 5V
GND (Brown/Black)      -> GND

PUSH BUTTON:
One leg                -> D3 / GPIO 0
Other leg              -> GND

HOW IT WORKS:
1. The feeder starts with the servo at 0 degrees.
2. Press the push button.
3. The servo rotates to 90 degrees and opens the food dispenser.
4. It stays open for 2 seconds.
5. The servo returns to 0 degrees and closes the dispenser.
6. The feeder waits for the next button press.

IMPORTANT:
- The code uses D5 and D3, matching the D1 Mini pin labels.
- For a larger/high-torque servo, use a separate suitable 5V power supply.
- Connect the external power supply GND to the D1 Mini GND.
- Do not power a high-current servo directly from the D1 Mini 5V pin.

lessons.name: Jackpot Running Light
lessons.description: Run four LEDs in sequence with 13 progressive speed stages for 30 seconds, then blink the final LED as the jackpot.
lessons.connectionGuide:
JACKPOT RUNNING LIGHT CONNECTION:

RED LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> D5 / GPIO 14
Cathode (-) -> GND

YELLOW LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> D6 / GPIO 12
Cathode (-) -> GND

GREEN LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> D7 / GPIO 13
Cathode (-) -> GND

BLUE LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> D3 / GPIO 0
Cathode (-) -> GND

OPERATION:
The four LEDs run in sequence for 30 seconds.
The starting LED is selected randomly.

13 SPEED STAGES:
0-3 sec   = 10 ms
3-6 sec   = 20 ms
6-9 sec   = 40 ms
9-12 sec  = 50 ms
12-15 sec = 80 ms
15-18 sec = 100 ms
18-21 sec = 200 ms
21-23 sec = 300 ms
23-25 sec = 500 ms
25-27 sec = 700 ms
27-28 sec = 900 ms
28-29 sec = 1200 ms
29-30 sec = 1500 ms

After the 30-second running sequence, the final LED is used as the jackpot LED.
The jackpot LED blinks 5 times for a total of approximately 5 seconds.

IMPORTANT:
Use a 220 ohm resistor for each LED.
Do not connect an LED directly to a GPIO pin without a current-limiting resistor.

lessons.name: Blink LED
lessons.description: Blink an LED using digital output.
lessons.connectionGuide:
LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> D5 / GPIO 14
Cathode (-) -> GND

The LED will blink every second.

lessons.name: Button Input
lessons.description: Read a push button and control an LED.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Push Button:
One leg -> D3 / GPIO 0
Other leg -> GND

LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> D5 / GPIO 14
Cathode (-) -> GND

The internal pull-up resistor is used.

lessons.name: Buzzer
lessons.description: Generate a tone using a buzzer.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Buzzer:
Positive (+) -> D6 / GPIO 12
Negative (-) -> GND

The buzzer produces a 1000 Hz tone for 500 milliseconds.

lessons.name: Serial Monitor
lessons.description: Display messages and analog readings in Serial Monitor.
lessons.connectionGuide:
No external components are required.

Connect the D1 Mini to the computer using USB.

Open Arduino IDE -> Tools -> Serial Monitor.
Set the baud rate to 115200.

lessons.name: Analog Input
lessons.description: Read an analog value from a potentiometer.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Potentiometer:
Middle pin -> A0

Connect the other two pins according to the voltage range supported by your D1 Mini board.

IMPORTANT: Check the A0 input voltage limit of your specific D1 Mini board before applying external voltage.

lessons.name: WiFi Connection
lessons.description: Connect the D1 Mini to a WiFi network.
lessons.connectionGuide:
No external components are required.

Before uploading, replace:
YOUR_WIFI_NAME
YOUR_WIFI_PASSWORD

with your WiFi network name and password.

Open Serial Monitor at 115200 baud to see the assigned IP address.

lessons.name: WiFi Web Server
lessons.description: Create a simple web server that controls an LED.
lessons.connectionGuide:
No external components are required if using the D1 Mini built-in LED on D5 in this example.

Replace the WiFi name and password in the code.

After uploading, open Serial Monitor at 115200 baud.

Copy the displayed IP address into a web browser connected to the same WiFi network.

lessons.name: Button Counter
lessons.description: Count button presses and display the count in Serial Monitor.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Push Button:
One leg -> D3 / GPIO 0
Other leg -> GND

The internal pull-up resistor is used.

Open Serial Monitor at 115200 baud to view the counter.
